item.title: Thermodynamic–Kinetic Coupling of Water Structure Enables Wide‐Temperature Zinc Batteries
item.description:

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in coupling thermodynamic and kinetic regulation of water structure via a hydrogel electrolyte that disrupts hydrogen bonding while restricting molecular dynamics. This simultaneously suppresses ice nucleation and hydrogen evolution, enabling wide-temperature zinc batteries. Significance: over 8000 h symmetric-cell stability, 15,000 full-cell cycles, and reversible operation at −30°C, offering a design strategy for extreme-condition aqueous batteries.

💡 The novelty lies in dual-regulating chlorine coordination to suppress passivation and enable reversible Zn–Cl chemistry. This yields a ~2 V zinc–chlorine battery operating at −60 °C with elevated capacity, overcoming the freezing and sluggish kinetics limits of aqueous electrolytes. It advances ultra-low-temperature energy storage and offers a design strategy for high-voltage, high-capacity cryogenic batteries.

💡 This study provides rare temperature-dependent dielectric data for real industrial LIB black mass, linking permittivity evolution to carbothermal reduction phases. It reveals that dielectric losses surge during layered-to-oxide transformation (500–650°C), with 910 MHz enabling uniform volumetric heating versus localized 2.45 GHz heating. These insights enable frequency-tuned microwave recycling optimization.

item.description:

Advanced Science | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in identifying cooling-driven oxygen-mediated reconstruction as a key synthetic lever controlling manganese vacancies and stacking faults in sodium manganese oxide cathodes. This challenges prior focus on pre-formed motifs. Its significance: kinetically regulating cooling enables a stacking-fault-rich architecture that suppresses Mn migration and irreversible oxygen release, establishing a general design principle for stabilizing oxygen-redox cathodes.
